interactions.summary: A student names J.D. Vance as another conflict-sower, and Jiang pushes back by asking whether that would make every politician equally guilty.
The conversation shifts from individual politicians to social media, and Jiang argues that algorithmic anger production makes Mark Zuckerberg a more fitting example of engineered discord.
Students float Greta Thunberg, media in general, and Nick Fuentes, while Jiang keeps narrowing the exercise toward naming concrete agents rather than abstract systems.

claims.claim: Jiang says social media algorithms are designed to provoke anger because anger drives engagement and keeps people using the platforms.
Jiang argues that Mark Zuckerberg can count as a modern sower of discord because social media replaces consensus-building with isolated bubbles and combative argument.
Jiang contrasts earlier mass media with platform culture by saying the evening news tried to build community and consensus, whereas social media rewards beating the other side.

Jiang keeps insisting on a personal agent rather than an abstract category, which implies that for this circle the responsibility must attach to identifiable makers of division rather than to 'media' in general.
claims.temporal_scope: Methodological pressure applied in class on 2026-06-24.

signature_moments.moment: Discord becomes a business model: anger is manufactured because an outraged person is a more valuable user.
signature_moments.source_phrase: they're trying to provoke anger because with anger you're much more engaged
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It translates Dante's moral category into a contemporary mechanism of algorithmic division.

signature_moments.moment: The old public square is replaced by bubbles that stop seeking consensus and start trying to beat the other guy.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you live in your own bubble
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's clearest description of how mediated schism reorganizes social life.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's way of mapping a modern platform architect onto Dante's category of those who organize division and antagonism.

uncertainty_notes.note: The transcript phrase 'every politician soils conflict' is likely ASR distortion of 'sows conflict'; downstream quote use should normalize carefully.
